item.title: SolarFCD: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Solar Fault Classification in Photovoltaic Systems
item.description:
Misbah Ijaz, Saif Ur Rehman Khan, Abd Ur Rehman, Arooj Zaib, Sebastian Vollmer, Andreas Dengel, Muhammad Nabeel Asim
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08412-8
Abstract The increasing global deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems needs robust, scalable, and automated inspection technologies capable of detecting a wide range of panel flaws under a variety of operating situations. The lack of comprehensive, multi-modal, publicly available annotated datasets is a major obstacle preventing advancement in this field. We introduce SolarFCD, a harmonized multi-modal dataset of solar panel defects created by methodically combining and reconciling three publicly accessible datasets covering two imaging modalities. Following near-duplicate removal, the dataset comprises 3,742 unique real images, expanded to 6,651 through targeted augmentation of the three under-represented classes; augmentation was applied to the training and validation partitions, and all test images are unique real observations. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and test splits at an 80:10:10 ratio through methodical label mapping, near-duplicate removal, and targeted augmentation of minority classes. Sixteen classification architectures from five design families were trained and assessed on the dataset to provide repeatable benchmark baselines. With an accuracy of 86.93%, precision of 88.79%, recall of 88.72%, and F1-score of 88.27%, ResNet101V2 performed the best overall. Per-class results showed balanced detection across all four defect categories within a narrow performance band. To promote open and repeatable research in automated PV inspection and solar energy operations and maintenance, the dataset, annotation files, and baseline code are made openly available.

item.title: Expanding the set of high-evidence drug-target interactions in the Cancer Targetome
item.description:
Daniel Bottomly, Nathaniel J. Evans, Shannon K. McWeeney
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08824-6
Abstract The development of clinically relevant biomarkers is facilitated by accurate, comprehensive maps of drug–target interactions (DTIs). However, existing DTI resources are fragmented, inconsistently stratified by evidence, and provide incomplete coverage of clinically used small-molecule drugs. Here we extend the Cancer Targetome into Targetome-expanded (T-E), an aggregated, evidence-aware DTI resource that integrates four major experimental and curated data sources and a rigorously filtered set of knowledge-graph–based predictions. T-E harmonizes more than 1.6 million DTI records and yields 4,143 clinically relevant small-molecule drugs with high-evidence interactions to 5,176 protein targets, representing a 21-fold and 6.8-fold increase, respectively, over the original Targetome while maintaining internal consistency (97% of drugs and 99% of comparable level III DTIs after harmonization). An evaluation of the top 10 predicted DTIs showed that the majority were supported by independent literature. T-E provides an open, standardized resource that improves actionable target coverage for umbrella trial arm nomination, enriches feature spaces for drug-response modeling, and supports systematic prioritization of rational combination therapies in precision oncology and pharmacogenomics studies.
